title_one_paragraph_one: Hässelby Strands Sjöscoutkår (HSS) is a traditional non-profit youth organization with a focus on scouting and boating. We are religiously and politically independent, and a member of the Swedish Scout Association, which with approximately 65,000 members is one of Sweden's largest youth organizations.
title_one_paragraph_two: The goal of our activities is to give children and young people the opportunity to experience nature, boating, seamanship, challenges and - above all - camaraderie. The basic idea is Learning by doing. Within the Scouts, there is no substitute bench.
title_one_paragraph_three: The Scout Group was founded in 1959 and operates from a cozy clubhouse (called Ruffen) on the shore of Lake Mälaren in Hässelby. The group has around 130 active members and owns five sailboats, ten Optimist dinghies, two 2-krona sailing boats, a fast support boat, and a large Scout cabin.
title_two_paragraph_one: On Sunday, January 28, 1968, Myset was officially opened. Myset is our cabin in Lövsta. At that time, HSS’s Parents’ Association had been working on the cabin for three years.
title_two_paragraph_two: The construction cost nearly 50,000 SEK, which was raised through bazaars and raffles. On the opening day, nearly 400 eager scouts and parents were present. They witnessed the chairman of the Parents’ Association, Agne Stavegren, formally hand over the key to the chairman of HSS, Lennart Carlbom.
title_three_paragraph_one: Ingalunda was a Plymsnäckan-type boat built at the Neglinge shipyard, most likely in the 1920s or 1930s. It was purchased in 1961 by the Drakarna patrol, which had been forced to scrap its sister vessel, Någorlunda. It carried 16 square meters of sail on a gaff rig. Built of clinker planking, it would heel readily, even though the bowsprit was not particularly high above the water. It is preserved in photographs. It was the first of the troop’s boats to be fitted with an engine, in 1963. That same year, Rubinen also received an engine. Most of the boats therefore remained without engines well into the 1970s.
